messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] sev2 - continuous-batcher queue drift detected in eu-west-1. Multiple pods hitting CUDA OOMs and restarting. Detected at 2026-03-15T10:15Z. Affected service: redwood-runtime-batcher. Autoscaler triggered restarts.

maya: ack, I'm on it. Observed steady growth in pending_batches metric for last 6m. Tracing shows batcher accepts requests faster than consumers are draining KV cache.

raj: looks like KV eviction pressure + large pad tokens increasing seq_len distribution. Dumping recent logs and top OOM traces:
```
[2026-03-15T10:13:22Z] OOM: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (device 0)
[2026-03-15T10:13:22Z] reaper: killing pod redwood-batcher-7f8d9 (node eu-west-1a)
[2026-03-15T10:14:01Z] continuous-batcher: queue_depth=9216 inflight=1024
```

alex: interjecting — customer-facing latency spike reported from billing-service and chatbot-routes. Support tracking 3 active customers with >5x latency, 2 with occasional 5xx.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle new batch ingress (rate-limit on proxy), 2) scale batcher consumers up temporarily to relieve queue, 3) mark node eu-west-1a unschedulable to stop repeated restarts. Anyone object?

lin: Can we do a config flip to reduce max_batch_size from 1024 -> 256? That would reduce memory per batch and likely stop OOMs.

raj: agree. Prep patch:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher MAX_BATCH_SIZE=256
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher
```

maya: applying throttle on edge proxy (rate-limit rule applied to /v1/generate):
```
proxyctl apply -f - <<EOF
- path: /v1/generate
  rate_limit: 600rps
EOF
```
proxyctl: rule accepted, effective in ~15s

inc-bot: automated action — scaled deployment continuous-batcher +3 replicas (reason: high-queue). New replica rollouts started.

maya: scaling confirmed. Restarting affected pod on eu-west-1a now to clear bad state.

raj: watch logs for backpressure, enable debug for kv-cache for 10m:
```
kubectl logs -f deploy/continuous-batcher -c runtime | grep kv-cache
```

maya: observed queue decrease from 9216 -> 1200 over 90s after throttle + scale + MAX_BATCH_SIZE flip. No further OOMs in last 3m. Latency for impacted customers dropping toward baseline.

lin: support note: notified customer A and B, they acknowledged. Created incident ticket INC-4321 with RCA placeholder.

emily: planning handoff in 30m. Summary for next oncall:
- root cause: continuous-batcher batch growth + high sequence lengths + kv-cache memory pressure triggering CUDA OOM -> pod restarts
- mitigations applied: proxy throttle, MAX_BATCH_SIZE=256, scaled replicas +3, cordoned node eu-west-1a
- customer impact: 3 customers saw 5x latency window ~10m, 2 customers intermittent 5xx. No data loss.
- next steps: monitor queue_depth, revert throttle once queue sustained <500 for 15m, follow-up RCA runbook: /wiki/rca/continuous-batcher

maya: handing over to emily for the 10:45-11:15 shift. drop any follow-ups here. :white_check_mark:

inc-bot: note — incident tagged sev2, incident channel created: #inc-4321-continuous-batcher-queue-drift
